## ⛔ Landing gate ② is blocked by a FALSE POSITIVE, and I am not clearing it the way the script says would clear it

Read at `2026-09-15T00:26Z`. `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9540` → **exit 4**:

> ✗ C5 — card #9309 (delivering open PR #9540 (draft)) declares `Clause-②: no` while its diff carries 1 widening tell(s) … `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1811` (T1)
> T1 … — **a new key on a Zod object schema — the accept set gains a spelling an author may now write** — `+ filter: z.union([`

**The tell's premise is false here, and the diff says so in the same hunk.** `git diff 4f0fbce38f 3e60765fb4a8 -- packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`:

```
 export const ObjectGallerySchema = BaseSchema.extend({
   type: z.literal('object-gallery'),
   objectName: z.string().optional().describe('ObjectQL object name'),
-  filter: z.unknown().optional().describe('Query filter, forwarded verbatim as $filter'),
+  … comment block …
+  filter: z.union([
```

⇒ `filter` is **replaced**, ⛔ not added. The matcher reads the `+` line without checking whether the same key left on a `-` line in the same hunk, so a replacement is scored as an addition.

**And the direction is inverted.** The removed spelling is `z.unknown()` — zod's **universal acceptor**. Every value the new union accepts was already accepted; some values accepted before (`'stage=won'`, `42`, per the dev's measurement, which the review seat is verifying independently) are now refused. ⇒ the accept set **shrinks**. The published TS face moves the same way, `unknown` → `QueryParams['$filter']`. Neither limb of `SKILL.md:476`'s disjunction fires — nothing is relaxed and nothing is widened — so **`Clause-②: no` stands as declared**.

**⛔ I am not re-declaring `yes`, and the script itself is why.** Its C5 docblock states the price of doing that, in its own words:

> ⚠️ A TELL, never a proof, in BOTH directions: a false negative is the cost the ruling accepted when it took the directional reading, and a false **POSITIVE is repaired in the matcher — ⛔ not paid for by the author**. This file priced it at "one word in the claim comment" until #16822 measured the price: the exit-0 condition is "no tell, OR the declaration is not `no`", so **the only word that clears a false tell is `Clause-②: no` → `yes` — a widening recorded in a governance ledger that did not happen, and afterwards indistinguishable from one that did.**

⇒ flipping the declaration would buy a green exit by writing a widening into the governance record that did not occur. The same docblock closes the other door too: *"⛔ Nothing about this row is relaxed by saying so: the exit stays non-zero and stays a hard block."*

**So the honest state of this PR is:** the change looks right and the review is running, but **gate ② cannot pass on my authority**, and I will not enqueue without it. This is not a defect in the diff and ⛔ nothing here is asked of the dev.

**What happens next**

1. A card is filed against the matcher in `objectstack` — the repair is that a `+` key whose same key appears on a `-` line in the same hunk is a **replacement**, and a replacement out of `z.unknown()` or `z.any()` cannot widen by construction. Linked from this PR once it exists.
2. Round-1 contract review is already running at this head; ① is independent of this and proceeds.
3. When the matcher is repaired, `--pair 9540` is re-run as the landing reading. If it still refuses, that is a real disagreement and goes to the maintainer, ⛔ not around the gate.

⚠️ For whoever reads this later: the `--pair` exit **stayed 4**. ⛔ Nothing in this comment clears it, and a green exit is not implied by anything above. The script is right to block; its matcher is what needs the fix.

## The matcher card is filed, and the false positive is now measured rather than argued

objectstack#18234 — filed bare and unassigned; routing and grading are triage's.

**What changed since the comment above: I stopped arguing the direction and measured the matcher.** Running `wideningTells(…, { repo: 'objectstack-ai/objectui' })` from `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs` on this diff and on four controls:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| this PR — `- filter: z.unknown()…` → `+ filter: z.union([` | **FIRES T1** |
| **the same removal** → `+ filter: z.array(z.any()).optional()…` | **declines** |
| a genuinely new key, nothing removed | FIRES ✅ |
| `z.enum(['a','b'])` → `z.enum(['a','b','c'])` | FIRES ✅ |
| `z.enum(['a','b','c'])` → `z.enum(['a','b'])` | declines ✅ |

⭐ Row 2 is the whole finding: **the same semantic change declines when the new value is spelled `z.array(z.any())` and fires when it is spelled `z.union([…])`.** Direction identical, spelling different. ⛔ That is not a reason to re-spell this PR to dodge the gate — the union is the right shape for a two-arm destination type, and re-spelling to please a matcher is the kind of thing that makes the next reader believe the matcher was right.

Root cause, read in the source: `#16943`'s replacement budget **is earned** here (the removed `filter:` line is T1-shaped and buys a T1 unit) and then refused at the **spend**, because the added line opens `z.union(`. `#17618` lets a closed-set-valued key spend only on *"a removed line naming the SAME key, both member lists readable on their own line, and the added list a SUBSET of the removed one"* — and the removed value `z.unknown()` **has no member list**, because it is not a closed set. It accepted the universe, so every replacement is a subset by construction; the three-fact test has no way to say that.

⚠️ Disclosed because it is the kind of thing this lane fails on: my **first** run of that probe was void — I called `wideningTells` without `{ repo }`, so every case declined including the two that must fire. An objectui path is off-surface when the repo defaults to objectstack. The table above is the re-run in which the controls fire.

**State of this PR is unchanged and stated plainly:** `--pair 9540` still exits 4, gate ② still does not pass, and this PR is **not** enqueued. Round-1 contract review is running at this head and is independent of all of the above.

## Contract review

Independent review seat for objectui#9540 at head `3e60765fb4a80c3ee5c098b8133a26533de39842` (card objectui#9309). Every figure below was re-derived on this seat's own instruments in a fresh clone; the card, the claim comment [`5672443215`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/9309#issuecomment-5672443215) and the dev report [`5672743091`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/9309#issuecomment-5672743091) were read as claims to test, not as findings to adopt. ⛔ No label hung, added or removed; no review submitted; nothing approved, merged, enqueued, undrafted, pushed or re-run.

**Merge-base derived here, not adopted.** The shared checkout's `origin/main` is stale at `1cca4415e`, so `main` was fetched from GitHub (`75fca9669a3df84b065c1e9ded0946d67112000d`) before measuring: `git merge-base 3e60765fb4 gh/main` → **`4f0fbce38f6f19fa0fb6e776afa0f1091d6dab9a`**. It happens to equal the API's `base.sha`; that is a result, not an input. Against it: **4 files, +334/−8, 1 commit** — confirmed by `git diff --numstat`.

**Claims tested: 26**, enumerated twice and agreeing (`wc -l` over the ledger → 26; distinct claim ids via `awk | sort -u` → 26). 22 confirmed, 1 refuted, 1 split, 1 sound-but-unmeasured, 1 confirmed-correct-against-policy. The population those claims range over — the `filter` declarations in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` — is **proved at 9** below by two independent enumerations that agree.

---

### 1. The census — 9 declarations, 4 spellings, counting rule beside the number

⭐ **Counting rule:** every `filter` property signature in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, charged to its owning interface by the **nearest enclosing `InterfaceDeclaration`**, ⛔ never by proximity to the nearest preceding `export interface` line. Optionality is recorded rather than assumed — and, measured, all 9 carry a `?`, so the "optional" qualifier in the dev's rule is currently vacuous and does not do any of the work. ⛔ No line numbers pinned in prose.

Two instruments, written independently of the PR's committed test and of each other:

- **A — TypeScript AST, owner resolved by walking PARENT POINTERS upward** from each `filter` property signature. Deliberately *not* the descent-carry algorithm the PR's test uses.
- **B — no TypeScript library at all**: blank out comment bodies and string/template literals preserving offsets, then brace-walk a stack of `interface <Name>` blocks.

Both print the same 9 rows, in the same order, with the same owners and spellings, at the merge-base and at head:

| owning interface | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ObjectGridSchema` | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| **`NamedListView`** | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectMapSchema` | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectGanttSchema` | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectCalendarSchema` | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectKanbanSchema` | `any[]` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectChartSchema` | `any[] \| Record<string, any>` | unchanged |
| `ObjectGallerySchema` | **`unknown`** | **`QueryParams['$filter']`** |
| `ObjectDataTableSchema` | `any` | `any` |

A third, cruder enumeration agrees: `grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*filter[[:space:]]*\??[[:space:]]*:' | wc -l` → **9** at both revisions (firing control on the same regex family: `objectName` → 11). Occurrence counts, ⛔ never `grep -c`: `filter?: any[];` → 6/6 · `filter?: unknown;` → 1 before / 0 after · `filter?: any;` → 1/1 · `filter?: QueryParams['$filter'];` → 0 before / 1 after. Base file length **4244 lines** — the seat's figure, reproduced.

**Firing control for the ownership rule.** A fixture where proximity and the parser disagree (`export interface Alpha { … }` closed, its name repeated in *prose*, then `export type Beta = { filter?: number }`, a member nested one object deep inside `Gamma`, a `filter?:` inside a block comment, and one inside a string literal). The proximity rule returns **5 rows** and charges `Beta`'s member to `Alpha`; both of my instruments return **3 rows** with that owner `undefined`, and both ignore the commented and the stringified one. The control fires, so the 9 is a reading.

⚠️ **A blind spot I found in my own instruments, and in the PR's:** all three resolve the key by identifier, so a *quoted* `'filter'?:` member would be missed. Closed separately — `grep -oE "['\"]filter['\"]\s*\??\s*:"` → **0**, with a same-file firing control (6 quoted keys of other names exist). So the zero is a reading, not a silence.

### 2. The card's comparative claim — the refutation is CONFIRMED, and is stronger than stated

The card's raw counts both reproduce (6 × `any[]`, 1 × `unknown`). The *framing* around them does not:

- The population of `filter` declarations is **9**, not the seven the card's "six siblings plus this one" implies. `ObjectChartSchema` (`any[] | Record<string, any>`) and `ObjectDataTableSchema` (`any`) are also not `any[]`, so `ObjectGallerySchema` was never "the one … that is not `any[]`".
- ⚠️ **`NamedListView` is confirmed not a view schema**, on evidence rather than on assertion: it is the only one of the 9 owners with **no `extends BaseSchema`** and **no `type: 'object-*'` literal discriminant** — its `type?` is `'grid' | 'kanban' | 'gallery' | …` and its own docblock says "Used in `ObjectViewSchema.listViews`". It is a nested named-view definition, not a widget node.
- ⇒ Restricted to actual view schemas, the true shape is: **8 of the 9 owners are view schemas, and only 5 of those 8 are `any[]`** (grid, map, gantt, calendar, kanban). So the card's "six" over-counts the array-only view schemas by one *and* under-counts the non-`any[]` ones by two, at the same time.

The defect itself survives untouched: `unknown` still promised a destination it did not type, and it was still the only one of the nine an author could not forward without asserting.

### 3. Direction — narrowing on both faces, measured with a control that fires

**TS face.** `unknown` is the top type, so any replacement narrows — but measured rather than asserted. A scratch probe under `tsconfig.test.json` asserted seven expected-accepted and four expected-refused assignments, plus one deliberate **unsuppressed** control. `tsc` exited 2 with **exactly one** diagnostic — the control:

```
error TS2322: Type '"this line must be TS2322"' is not assignable to type 'Record<string, any> | FilterArray | undefined'.
```

So the four `@ts-expect-error` silences (`string`, `42`, `null`, `unknown`) were used, and the seven acceptances (`any[]`, `Record<string, any>`, `ListViewSchema['filter']`, `undefined`, `[['status','=','active']]`, `{ age: { $gt: 18 } }`) are readings. Probe deleted; `git status --porcelain` empty afterwards.

**Zod face.** ⛔ Not assumed from "`z.unknown()` is the universal acceptor" — measured on the pinned **zod 4.4.3** over 11 samples. `z.unknown().optional()` **accepted all 11**, functions and `Date` included (that is the control for the acceptor claim, and it fired). The new union accepts `undefined`, `[]`, `[['status','=','active']]`, `{}`, `{ age: { $gt: 18 } }` and refuses `null`, `'stage=won'`, `42`, `true`, `Date`, function. A second control (`z.never()`) refused everything. ⇒ **strictly fewer values accepted at runtime, on both faces.** The dev's `filter: 'stage=won'` / `filter: 42` claim holds in both directions — see §5 for the proof that they *used* to compile.

**Arm order.** The comment's factual half is true: `ObjectChartSchema.filter` above is spelled with the identical two arms in the identical order.
